corrected_defects_in_v1_4.defect: V1.4 wrote 'singular values s_i <= 1e-15 are treated as exactly zero' into the Ridge SVD contract. The operator preregistered solver='svd' but never preregistered any singular-value cutoff, pseudoinverse tolerance or rank-determination threshold. The V1.4 author introduced it, creating an arbitrary project-defined numeric knob capable of changing a fitted coefficient vector.
corrected_defects_in_v1_4.resolution: WITHDRAWN. No project-side cutoff, tolerance or rank threshold of any kind. The pinned library estimator's internal numerical handling is the contract, fixed by the runtime version pin.

corrected_defects_in_v1_4.defect: V1.4 recorded that scikit-learn was absent from every interpreter and that no ML library was pinned, leaving the candidate-model runtime undefined and the Logistic path unimplementable.
corrected_defects_in_v1_4.resolution: candidate_model_runtime pinned: python 3.12.x + scikit-learn 1.9.0 in an isolated project virtual environment, with a mandatory full dependency freeze manifest.

ridge.objective_function: minimize over (w, c) of: ||y - X w - c*1||^2 + alpha * ||w||^2
objective_notes: residual sum of squares is NOT divided by n
alpha > 0 for every grid point, so the objective is strictly convex and the minimiser is unique
ridge.v1_4_withdrawn_statement: singular values s_i <= 1e-15 are treated as exactly zero (sklearn _solve_svd convention)
ridge.numerical_semantics_note: whatever Ridge(solver='svd') does internally about near-singular directions is part of the pinned library's semantics, fixed by the runtime version pin; it is not restated, overridden, replicated or configured by this project
ridge.tuning_objective_formula: MAE(alpha) = (1/K) * sum |y_val - yhat_val| over the K inner LOOCV splits
ridge.iterative_convergence_policy_note: svd is a direct (non-iterative) method; MODEL_NOT_FIT_OPTIMIZER_DID_NOT_CONVERGE does not apply to Ridge

logistic.objective_function: minimize over (w, c) of: 0.5 * w^T w + C * sum_i log(1 + exp(-ytilde_i * (x_i^T w + c))), with ytilde_i = 2*y_i - 1 in {-1,+1}
objective_notes: LARGER C = WEAKER regularization; this is why smallest C is the stronger-regularization tie-break
the L2 term makes the objective strictly convex and coercive, so a finite unique minimiser exists even under perfect class separation
logistic.reference_implementation: sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=<selected>, penalty='l2', solver='lbfgs', fit_intercept=True, class_weight=None, max_iter=10000, tol=1e-10)
logistic.negative_class_definition: official close <= IPO price (existing TIE_IS_ZERO_AT_OR_BELOW_IPO rule, unchanged)
logistic.tuning_objective_formula: Brier(C) = (1/K) * sum (p_i - y_i)^2 over the K inner LOOCV splits, p_i = predicted probability of class 1

single_class_policy.condition: outer training fold contains a single class

residual_items.item: BLAS/LAPACK backend and thread configuration are a byte-level reproducibility factor
residual_items.detail: SVD and the LBFGS gradient path run through the numpy/scipy BLAS/LAPACK backend; backend identity and thread count can change results in the last floating-point bits, which matters here only because hyperparameter ties turn on bit-exact score equality
residual_items.reason_not_frozen: freezing a thread count or BLAS backend would be exactly the kind of unauthorized numeric knob the Ridge cutoff withdrawal exists to remove
residual_items.required_action: the dependency manifest must record the BLAS/LAPACK backend, version and thread configuration actually in use; the implementation audit should treat cross-machine bit-level divergence as an open recorded risk
